EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a typical pattern of a small aliphatic molecule with no O–H (no band > 3100 cm⁻¹). 1) Strong doublet at 2939/2881 cm⁻¹ and the 1454 cm⁻¹ band are classic C-H stretches and CH₂/CH₃ bends found in ethyl groups. 2) A medium band at 1032 cm⁻¹ corresponds well to the C–N stretch of a trialkylamine; ethers would give C–O stretches slightly higher (1060–1150 cm⁻¹). 3) The 754 cm⁻¹ and 829 cm⁻¹ peaks match CH₂ rocking/wagging modes of ethyl groups found in triethylamine (reported Raman bands near 746 and 815 cm⁻¹). 4) The 1281 cm⁻¹ peak fits the CH₂ twist in trialkylamines (≈ 1280–1300 cm⁻¹). No bands diagnostic of isocyanate (≈ 2270 cm⁻¹) or hydroxyl groups are present, excluding candidates with N=C=O or –OH. Among the OH-free options, the complete set of ethyl-group bands uniquely matches CCN(CC)CC (triethylamine).
